aiAudit.reason: The diff replaces a per-test `TcpNioConnectionSupport` mock with a field re-initialized to a fresh mock in @BeforeEach, which is the intended promotion pattern. No stubbing, argument matcher or answer exists on this mock, and the only assertions are identity checks (`isSameAs`) against the same instance passed to `connectionSupport(...)` in each test, so no test can now pass for a different reason. Because @BeforeEach creates a new instance per test case, there is no cross-test sharing of accumulated interactions or mutable state and no execution-order dependency. Both call sites were actually replaced, so the duplication was genuinely removed.

Neither test asserts on accumulated interactions or mutable state of the Session mock itself; the only verification, 'Mockito.verify(sessionFactory, Mockito.times(2)).getSession();', targets sessionFactory, which is still created locally in the test body. Both call sites were actually replaced, so the duplication was genuinely removed.

aiAudit.reason: The new private helper `createMockSession(Map<String, TestLsEntry[]> listResults)` creates a fresh `Session` mock per invocation (`Session session = mock(Session.class);`) and re-establishes exactly the same per-path stubs by iterating the supplied map (`when(session.list(entry.getKey())).thenReturn(entry.getValue());`), so no stub, matcher or argument binding is dropped or weakened and no mock instance is shared across tests. All 11 tests reported as sharing the `session.list(...)` stubbing (testLs, testLs_f, testLs_f_R, testLs_f_R_dirs, testLs_None, testLs_1, testLs_1_f, testLs_1_dirs, testLs_1_dirs_links, testLs_1_a_f_dirs_links, testLs_1_a_f_dirs_links_filtered) have their inline `mock(Session.class)` + `when(session.list(...)).thenReturn(...)` lines replaced by a `createMockSession(...)` call, so the duplication was genuinely removed rather than only abstracted. The only incidental changes are statement reordering (e.g. computing `files`/`level1..level3` before the mock) and the use of `Map.of`/`singletonMap`/`HashMap`, which is safe because the stubbed keys are distinct literals, so map iteration order cannot alter matching.

aiAudit.reason: The extracted helper `createMockFolder` calls `mock(folderClass)` on every invocation, so no mock instance is shared between test cases. Each stubbing it absorbs is byte-for-byte equivalent to the original: `given(folder.getPermanentFlags()).willReturn(new Flags(Flags.Flag.USER))`, `given(folder.isOpen()).willReturn(true)`, and `willAnswer(invocation -> messages).given(folder).search(any(SearchTerm.class))`, with the `messages` array now supplied as a parameter holding the same value the lambda previously captured. The one test-specific extra stub, `given(folder.exists()).willReturn(true)` in testIdleChannelAdapterException, is retained at the call site, and the mock class is still `IMAPFolder.class` there because the class is passed through. All five listed call sites were replaced by `createMockFolder(...)`, so the duplication was genuinely removed; the reordering of the `folderField`/`storeField` reflection setup is call-order irrelevant since `adapter.start()` and `receiver.receive()` still run last.

All three duplicated mock-creation/stubbing pairs in each of the two test methods are replaced by helper calls, so the duplication is genuinely removed; no mock becomes a shared field, and no state accumulates across test cases. The reflective invocation merely reaches the same zero-arg method on the same mock class (SmbFile) used before (mock(SmbFile.class) / target-typed mock()). Anything the reflective call could break would surface as an IllegalStateException, not as a silently passing test, and the verification already reports identical pass/fail outcomes.

aiAudit.reason: The diff promotes a duplicated, unstubbed mock (WebServiceMessageSender) into a class-level field initialized in @BeforeEach and replaces both original creation sites and both usages. Each test still receives a fresh mock because JUnit 5 creates a new test instance and runs @BeforeEach per test method, so no mock instance is shared across test cases. The only assertions on it are identity checks (`isSameAs(webServiceMessageSender)`) in both marshallingOutbound and simpleOutbound, with no stubbing, no argument matchers, and no accumulated-interaction or mutable-state assertions, so outcomes cannot depend on execution order. The extra construction in the four tests that do not use the mock is a pre-existing/expected property of this refactoring, and the duplication was genuinely removed (no call site left using the old local `messageSender`).
